subject: Context safety-net: minimums, rounding and surcharge scenarios
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@orchard.ai>, Orchard.ai Procurement <procurement@orchard.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Context safety-net: minimums, rounding and surcharge scenarios

Elena / team,

Thanks again for walking through the pilot scope yesterday. We want to make the billing behavior during early usage transparent so you can model cost and procurement language. Two points to confirm so we align on contract language:

1) Microcalls and minimums: for very short calls (<= 32 tokens generated) we apply a microfloor of 1 billing unit. That avoids excessive fractional line-items.
2) Rounding windows: billing windows are per-session and rounded up to the nearest billing quantum (default 64-token quantum for this SKU).

Quick examples attached (orchard-metering-examples.csv) — there are three rows that map sample calls to invoice line math.

Questions for you:
- Do you have a procurement constraint against "round-up" billing (some customers require per-token exactness)?
- Would Orchard prefer a smoothing credit for the first month while traffic patterns stabilize?

I'll also loop in finance for a one-time concession if needed. If helpful, we can propose a safety-net clause that caps microfloor exposure for the pilot.

Attachments: orchard-metering-examples.csv

Best,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0132

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@orchard.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Orchard.ai Procurement <procurement@orchard.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Context safety-net: minimums, rounding and surcharge scenarios

Ben — thanks for the clear examples. A couple of clarifying items from my side:

- Procurement: our standard T&Cs push for per-token accuracy on invoices; round-ups are acceptable if they are limited and disclosed.
- Pilot ask: we want to avoid an unexpected $/minute surcharge on low-frequency user flows. Any smoothing / crediting approach would be appreciated.

Also can you add a sample invoice line showing multiple microcalls aggregated over a day (we bill internal teams weekly and need the visibility)? The CSV helps but a formatted invoice example will make legal happy.

Elena
Head of Product | Orchard.ai
elena.ruiz@orchard.ai | +1 212 555 0199

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@orchard.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Orchard.ai Procurement <procurement@orchard.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Context safety-net: minimums, rounding and surcharge scenarios

On Tue, May 30, 2028 at 09:12 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Elena / team,
>
> Thanks again for walking through the pilot scope yesterday. We want to make the billing behavior during early usage transparent so you can model cost and procurement language.

Hi Elena — adding a few concrete invoice lines below and attaching a pdf with the formatted example (20280530-proposal-v2.pdf).

Invoice example (daily aggregate):
- 2028-05-12: 18 microcalls (each 18 tokens generated), raw tokens = 324 -> billed as 18 * 1 unit (microfloor) = 18 units -> line item: 18 units x $0.015 = $0.27
- 2028-05-13: 3 long calls (avg 420 tokens) -> tokens round-up to nearest 64-quantum -> billed units = 3 * ceil(420/64) = 3 * 7 = 21 units

Notes:
- Microfloor applies per-call but we can apply an optional daily cap: cap the number of microfloor units to N% of total tokens per day for the pilot (example: cap at 15% of billed units).
- For streaming sessions, we bill based on emitted tokens; partial-minute streaming is prorated to token quantum.

Attached: 20280530-proposal-v2.pdf (formatted invoice example), orchard-metering-examples.csv

If Procurement prefers, we can present two wording options: (A) full transparency with round-up math and sample invoices, or (B) smoothing credit: Redwood issues a monthly credit to offset microfloor overcharges up to an agreed threshold.

Kimberly Park
Head of Pricing & Packaging | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@orchard.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Context safety-net: minimums, rounding and surcharge scenarios

Ben / team — quick operational note from finance/legal: we can offer a 30-day "safety-net" concession for pilots where Redwood absorbs microfloor overage above a de minimis threshold (e.g., total microfloor charge < $50 in month -> Redwood credit).

If Orchard wants something more contractually explicit we can:
- add a clause that caps microfloor billing exposure for the first 90 days, or
- agree a monthly smoothing credit computed against the first invoice.

I've attached a short term-sheet with the wording we typically use (concession-term-sheet.docx). This keeps procurement comfortable and requires minimal redlines.

Marissa Cole
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@orchard.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jake Morris <jake@contractsplus.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Context safety-net: minimums, rounding and surcharge scenarios

Elena — great, thanks for the quick replies. Proposed next steps:

1) I will send an updated proposal that:
   - includes the formatted sample invoice lines (attached PDF),
   - introduces the 30-day safety-net credit language (term sheet attached), and
   - adds an explicit daily microfloor cap example you can sign off.
2) Can we set a 30-minute legal/procurement sync on Friday to walk the clause? 11:00am PT works on our side.

If Procurement wants per-token exact invoicing as a hard requirement, we can expose that as an alternate SKU (per-token meter, no microfloor) — pricing will be slightly higher since we lose the quantum optimization.

I've attached the updated proposal and the example invoice: 20280530-proposal-v2.pdf, orchard-metering-examples.csv, concession-term-sheet.docx

Appreciate the collaboration — I think this will be an easy pilot to operationalize.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
